biological.citation: Dominantly acting KIF5B variants with pleiotropic cellular consequences cause variable clinical phenotypes (PMID: 36018820)
biological.summary: Three dominantly acting KIF5B variants (p.Asn255del, p.Leu498Pro, p.Leu537Pro) were identified in patients with phenotypes ranging from dilated cardiomyopathy with ophthalmoplegia to neurodevelopmental conditions with hypotonia. In vitro analyses showed these variants disrupt lysosomal, autophagosome, and mitochondrial organization and impact cilium biogenesis. All variants also affected multiple developmental processes in zebrafish in vivo.

biological.citation: Motor protein KIF5B inhibition as a novel strategy of controlled reperfusion against myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (PMID: 40057204)
biological.summary: KIF5B transports GLUT4- and CD36-containing vesicles to the plasma membrane, facilitating glucose and fatty acid import into cardiomyocytes. Genetic inhibition of KIF5B using AAV9-shRNA attenuated myocardial I/R injury, reducing infarct size, cardiac biomarkers, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and arrhythmias. Pharmacological inhibition with rose bengal lactone (1 mg/kg) also conferred cardioprotection, and siRNA knockdown of Kif5b inhibited fatty acid uptake in primary neonatal rat cardiomyocytes.

biological.citation: Hypertrophy induced KIF5B controls mitochondrial localization and function in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes (PMID: 27094714)
biological.summary: KIF5B gene and protein expression were elevated in neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes stimulated with phenylephrine (pathological hypertrophy model) but not with IGF1 (physiological hypertrophy model). KIF5B expression was also elevated in animal models of pathological cardiac hypertrophy in vivo. Silencing of Kif5b reverted peripheral mitochondrial localization and diminished PE-induced increases in mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate, demonstrating KIF5B's role in mitochondrial localization and function.

biological.citation: Endophilin A2 controls touch and mechanical allodynia via kinesin-mediated Piezo2 trafficking (PMID: 38475827)
biological.summary: KIF5B was identified as a binding partner of EndoA2 (endophilin A2) in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, forming a KIF5B/EndoA2/Piezo2 complex essential for anterograde membrane trafficking of the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo2. Loss of EndoA2 in NF200+ DRG neurons impaired Piezo2-mediated rapidly adapting mechanically activated currents and tactile/mechanical allodynia. KIF5B's role as a kinesin motor was shown to be indispensable for EndoA2-mediated Piezo2 trafficking to the plasma membrane.

biological.citation: The cohesin-associated protein Pds5A governs the meiotic spindle assembly via deubiquitination of Kif5B in oocytes (PMID: 40215310)
biological.summary: Pds5A recruits the deubiquitinase USP14 to the spindle apparatus in mouse oocytes to stabilize KIF5B protein, which is required for spindle elongation during meiosis. Morpholino-based depletion or genetic ablation of Pds5A led to defects in spindle organization and chromosome euploidy, effects linked to destabilization of KIF5B. This reveals a post-translational (deubiquitination) mechanism regulating KIF5B stability specifically during oocyte meiosis.

biological.citation: Ubiquitin-like processing of TUG proteins as a mechanism to regulate glucose uptake and energy metabolism in fat and muscle (PMID: 36246906)
biological.summary: In adipocytes, insulin-stimulated endoproteolytic cleavage of TUG generates TUGUL, a ubiquitin-like modifier that specifically modifies KIF5B kinesin motor. TUGUL-modified KIF5B then carries GLUT4 storage vesicles and other cargoes to the cell surface, linking KIF5B to the insulin-regulated glucose uptake pathway. This mechanism is cell-type specific, occurring in fat and muscle but not fibroblasts.

biological.citation: FOXA2 and STAT5A regulate oncogenic activity of KIF5B-RET fusion (PMID: 36895965)
biological.summary: KIF5B-RET fusion cells showed increased expression of RET and downstream signaling molecules (p-BRAF, p-ERK, p-AKT) and elevated nuclear p-STAT5A and FOXA2, with FOXA2 expression being much higher in RET-rearranged NSCLC (94.4%) than in RET wild-type NSCLC (45.0%). KIF5B-RET fusion cells demonstrated increased proliferation in xenograft mouse models and altered cell cycle profiles. FOXA2 siRNA knockdown in KIF5B-RET fusion cells reduced TGF-β1 mRNA but increased Twist1 and Snail, indicating FOXA2 regulates downstream oncogenic transcriptional programs.

biological.citation: A dual role of ERGIC-localized Rabs in TMED10-mediated unconventional protein secretion (PMID: 38926505)
biological.summary: KIF5B collaborates with Rab2A to regulate ERGIC compartmentalization, establishing a UcPS-specific compartment for unconventional protein secretion (UcPS) via TMED10. This identifies KIF5B as a motor protein involved in the spatial organization of the ERGIC during non-canonical secretory pathway activity. The study places KIF5B in a Rab2A-dependent regulatory axis distinct from conventional ER-to-Golgi trafficking.

biological.citation: m6A-modified circCCAR1 promotes malignant proliferation by enhancing KIF5B expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 40696234)
biological.summary: KIF5B mRNA is a direct target of miR-641, and circCCAR1 acts as a molecular sponge for miR-641 to relieve its inhibition of KIF5B in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells. CircCCAR1 also binds PTBP1 to stabilize KIF5B mRNA, resulting in significantly elevated KIF5B expression in HCC cell lines compared to normal hepatic cells. Silencing circCCAR1 suppressed HCC proliferation and tumor growth in xenograft models, effects partially reversed by KIF5B overexpression.

biological.citation: DNA double-strand break-capturing nuclear envelope tubules drive DNA repair (PMID: 38632359)
biological.summary: KIF5B, together with KIF13B, collaborates with the LINC complex, NUP153, nuclear lamina, DDR kinases, and ATAT1-acetylated cytoplasmic microtubules to generate DSB-capturing nuclear envelope tubules (dsbNETs) that localize to DNA double-strand breaks and promote their repair. dsbNETs are reversed by kinesin KIFC3, indicating KIF5B drives their formation. These structures are hyper-induced in cells expressing the aging-linked lamin A mutant progerin and are co-opted during PARP inhibition in BRCA1-deficient breast cancer cells.
